polyarticular inflammatory arthritis involving the wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, and proximal interphalangeal joints
fatigue
dyspnea on exertion
5-7 kg weight loss
no fever or sweats

concepts.why: The presence of pink-purple dermal papules, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes, along with a low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal, are characteristic of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

The presence of pink-purple dermal papules, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes, along with a low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal, and the involvement of the skin and lymph nodes, are characteristic of Sézary syndrome.
The presence of polyarticular inflammatory arthritis and the relief of symptoms with prednisone are consistent with psoriatic arthritis, although the skin findings are not typical of psoriasis.

The presence of polyarticular inflammatory arthritis and the relief of symptoms with prednisone are consistent with rheumatoid arthritis, although the skin findings are not typical of rheumatoid arthritis.

The presence of pink-purple dermal papules and a nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate are characteristic of lymphomatoid papulosis, although the clinical course and other findings are not typical of this condition.

The presence of polyarticular inflammatory arthritis, fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and weight loss are consistent with adult-onset Still's disease, although the skin findings and other features are not typical of this condition.

rationales.F02: Polyarticular inflammatory arthritis is common in psoriatic arthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
rationales.F09: Nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate is a hallmark of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F10: Admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes are characteristic of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F11: Low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal are characteristic of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and Sézary syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of pink-purple dermal papules, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and admixed atypical lymphocytes with a low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal, along with clonal T-cell receptor rearrangements in skin and bone marrow, strongly supports Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Sézary syndrome is a close runner-up but is less likely due to the absence of lymphadenopathy.
